Sampled ranking metrics can change model ordering: Hidasi and Czapp (2023) demonstrate reversals under negative sampling, supporting auxiliary candidate-pool sensitivity checks without changing the pinned evaluator. Prakash et al. (2024) show aggregate sequential-recommendation accuracy can hide head/mid/tail disparities. Report ranking errors by training-frequency bands, with group counts; compare fixed auxiliary candidate pools of different sizes and sampling distributions. These measure evaluation sensitivity and popularity-conditioned performance, respectively. [Sampling pitfalls](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/eval_flaws_recsys23.pdf), [popularity-stratified experiments](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276).

Guo et al. (ICML 2024) identify embedding collapse as occupation of a low-dimensional subspace. Motivated by this, inspect centered item embeddings and appended-mask user representations using singular-value spectra and effective rank, explicitly defining spectral normalization and excluding padding/mask tokens from item statistics. Low rank alone does not establish poor recommendations; separately measure full-catalog unseen-item top-10 coverage, exposure entropy, Gini and head-item share. Proposed calibration controls: progressively truncate representation rank, blend user representations toward their mean, shuffle valid history items, and add a temporary popularity-dependent score perturbation. These are diagnostic interventions on the same model, not deployed predictors; verify each probe’s dose response and unintended sensitivities. [Embedding-collapse study](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v235/guo24e.html).

Ekstrand et al. (2024) emphasize distributions and uncertainty beyond point estimates. Practical adaptation: paired user-level bootstrap within each category, then recompute the four-category macro average; keep candidate pools fixed to separate user uncertainty from sampling variability. Cache scores, bound diagnostic users and perturbation levels, and reuse bootstrap indices. Keep every probe auxiliary to unchanged host HR@10; these controls calibrate interpretations rather than establish causal diagnoses. [Distributionally-informed evaluation](https://841.io/doc/disteval.pdf).
